get.description:
Server-sent events, in order, each with an `id` (a reconnecting browser resumes after the
last one it saw): `queued` (`{ask_id, position}`, again whenever the position changes),
`retrieving`, `answering` (`{ask_id}`), then one of `answer` (an `AskResponse`), `error` (an
`AskErrorOut`) or `cancelled`. The stream ends after that one. A comment line is sent every
15 seconds so proxies keep the connection open. A plain `GET`: the browser's `EventSource`
sends the session cookie, and no CSRF header is needed because nothing changes. The session
is checked again before the `answer` is sent: a browser that signed out, or whose session
ended, while the question was being answered gets no answer and the stream just ends.

put.description:
Owner or admin, drafts only. `422` lists each problem with a JSON pointer into the item.
An item that people have already decided on (accept, edit or reject) keeps its text: the
answer is `409` with the type `item-has-decisions`, because those decisions are about the
text they read. Put the change in an `edit` decision, which is applied at the freeze.

post.description:
Any member may review any item of a draft, with the `etag` of the draft they read in
`If-Match`: a decision is about the text that was read, so it is refused when the draft has
changed since. The file is append only: a new decision replaces yours, it never edits it.
`edit` and `reject` need a `note`; an `edit` lists the item fields to replace and is applied
when the draft is frozen.
